text:
Neos has two avenues for generating Return of Capital (ROC). Tax loss harvesting when rolling options, at or prior to expiration, can recharacterize income distributions from unfavorable sources such as ordinary income or short term gains to ROC. The 1256 60/40 Long/Short tax treatment isn't really used to pass along long term gains. Rather, this is another method that Neos uses to carry losses over in the ETF that can again be used to recharacterize income distributions as ROC.

Neos' Garrett has stated in an interview with another YouTuber that they can structure their Flex Options on cash-settled ETF options to make them 1256-eligible, as seems to be the case with the GLD options in IAUI.

For taxable accounts, qualified dividends and long term capital gains are taxed at more favorable rates, but are still included in Adjusted Gross Income (AGI), and thus also in Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI). However, ROC is NOT included in AGI, as well as MAGI. MAGI is used in calculations for things like: 1) Eligibility for various tax credits and deductions; 2) Effects on Roth or Traditional IRA contributions; 3) Qualifications for Affordable Care Act (ACA) subsidies or Medicaid eligibility; and 4) Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount (IRMAA) Medicare Surcharge tiers for the two-year lookback of investors aged 63 and older.

text: You missed one of the major fundamental flaws in a covered call fund. When the underlying declines, they continue to follow their playbook to provide a continual steady stream of income to you. What that means, when SPY, QQQ, TSLA, whatever your fund is working off (or a basket of underlyings in the case of something like ULTY) declines in value, they still continue to sell ATM, OTM or whatever their strategy is and as that underlying recovers, you end up getting capped along the way. You will always eventually end up with less NAV then you started with through a complete market cycle. This is why NEOS (who provides the funds mentioned) and many others offers products like their Hedged Equity Income funds or specific strategies to hedge this condition but they return in the single digits. You could protect yourself by running a DIY opportunity hedge upfront and deploying that capital at market lows or putting on second layers of alpha as the market is recovering. You could also run a DIY strategy and control the upside rolls if tested to get back to basis and still make income.
